reason: The question about contact details for incident reporting and roles responsible for communications with CSIRT Italia has the selected answer that neither contact details nor responsible people are identified. AR-05 confirms this self-report: Aurora Grid has identified neither a point of contact and deputy nor a CSIRT liaison and deputies, and it has no staffed incident-reporting channel. The self-report and dossier are therefore consistent, and neither is more favourable. GV.RR-02_P3 requires the cybersecurity organisation to include those designated roles and alternates; their explicit absence is a failure of the central requirement. AR-05 also states that no management-approved and internally communicated cybersecurity organisation exists, consistent with the organisational context in GV.RR-02_P1. The incident plan's phases, notification and reporting provisions do not cure the failure because it lacks contact details and internal or external communication methods (AR-05). Likewise, operational continuity contacts in AR-14 and supplier relationship contacts in AR-11 are expressly not incident-reporting channels or designated CSIRT Italia contacts. This conclusion is also consistent with the implementation guidance on assigning security responsibilities and authorities (V5-ENISA-0004-01) and maintaining effective incident communication arrangements, assigned roles and contact lists (V5-ENISA-0010-01), although that guidance does not itself prove Aurora Grid's implementation. The precise contents of the referenced Article 7(6) determination were not supplied, but that limitation does not prevent the verdict because every role expressly named in GV.RR-02_P3 is documented as absent (AR-05).
missing_information: The text of the determination adopted pursuant to Article 7(6) of the NIS Decree was not supplied, so any specifications it adds beyond the roles expressly stated in GV.RR-02_P3 cannot be assessed.
